podcast.title: Accusation of Crystal Meth Use Against Noel (1994)
podcast.body: After Noel Gallagher left the first North American tour with $8,000 of the band's money following a fight, Liam accused Noel of taking the band's crystal meth with him. This comment highlighted the band's drug use during that period and the underlying animosity between the brothers. "But I think he took the band of crystal meth with him as well as the money."

podcast.title: Crystal Meth Use Confession (1994)
podcast.body: Liam Gallagher admitted that the entire band, including him and Noel, were heavily using crystal meth during their chaotic 1994 North American tour, which contributed to the backstage and on-stage incidents. He also accused Noel of taking a bag of crystal meth along with the band's money when he temporarily left the tour. "I don't remember much about it. I remember like just being a king, and I remember like, I remember one of our oldest girls. It was like, just going, I got some of this stuff there, you want to go there to do it out, you want to give it a go. And we were doing it, we thought it was cold-kay, or whatever, and we didn't kind of consume it, we'd throw the sh**y gig, so sh**y and whacked it and sh**y gigs, smoking weed, we don't sh**y gigs before, or what a big fuss was about. But obviously, it caused scene and Noel left and then went back. Noel had enough of a month somewhere else, but you know, I think he took the bag of crystal meth with him, as well as the money, so he's pretty much the same geezer, that was chopping it out, so we can't have it out, actually, you can't have it out, sh**ing, it just goes through by it."

podcast.title: On-stage Provocations (1994 North American Tour)
podcast.body: During Oasis's first North American tour in the fall of 1994, Liam frequently annoyed Noel by changing the lyrics of Noel's songs to offensive words, such as "Maybe I don't really want to know why you pick your nose" during "Live Forever." "Noel locked the studio doors and no one could get in, which really embarrassed Liam."

podcast.title: Cathay Pacific Ban (1998)
podcast.body: In March 1998, Liam Gallagher was banned from Cathay Pacific due to a severe air rage incident on a flight from Hong Kong to Perth, Australia. The altercation reportedly began over a scone and escalated to him smoking, swearing at the flight crew, and throwing items around the cabin. The captain had to intervene, threatening to divert the flight and remove Liam, the rest of Oasis, and their 30-member entourage if the disruptive behavior continued. Liam has since stated his preference to walk to Australia rather than fly with Cathay Pacific again. "Today, Liam says that he'd rather walk to Australia than fly Cathay, which I don't think will be much of a problem."

xref.title: Brit Pop Rivalry with Blur (1995)
xref.body: Oasis was deeply involved in an intense rivalry with Blur, described as a "war" between "Brit Pop's two biggest stars," which significantly hyped the release of Oasis's second album. The conflict began with a near-fight at a San Francisco radio station and escalated when Liam Gallagher and Damon Albarn almost brawled backstage at an award ceremony. Damon Albarn intentionally advanced Blur's single release date to coincide with Oasis's, culminating in the "Record War" of August 14, 1995, involving "Roll With It" versus "Country House," a battle that captivated all of Britain's music and daily papers, with even bookmakers taking bets. "This was much more than a rivalry. This was a war."

Huitt subsequently auctioned the bat, complete with a certificate of authenticity, for approximately a thousand US dollars. "He later auctioned it off, complete with a certificate of authenticity. And I think it sold for about a thousand US dollars."

xref.title: Liam Gallagher Bails on US Flight (August 27, 1996)
xref.body: Four days after the chaotic MTV Unplugged taping, on August 27, 1996, Liam Gallagher abruptly abandoned a British Airways flight bound for America. He demanded his bags be removed just ten minutes before takeoff, stating he wasn't going, further exacerbating the band's internal strife and public image issues. "Four days later, when the entire band was already on a British airways flight bound for America, Liam suddenly bailed. He was in his seat. Ten minutes before takeoff, he said, not take my bags off, I'm not going anywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liam Gallagher's Absence from MTV Unplugged Vocals (August 23, 1996)
xref.body: On the night of the MTV Unplugged taping, August 23, 1996, Liam Gallagher refused to sing, claiming a sore throat, leading Noel Gallagher to handle all the vocals. Liam was observed in a balcony, drinking beer and heckling Noel, causing fury from MTV due to the wasted time and expense. "Nole and Liam came to blows several times, and when the night of the taping arrived, which was August 23, 1996, Liam said, not can't sing tonight, I have a sore throat. But rather than cancel, the show went on, with Nole handling all the vocals. Liam, meanwhile, was seen up in a balcony, drinking beer and heckling Nole. MTV was furious all this time and expense ruined by Liam's little drama play."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: MTV Music Video Awards Performance – Deliberate Off-Key Singing (September 4, 1996)
xref.body: At the MTV Music Video Awards in New York, Liam Gallagher deliberately sang off-key and made annoyed gestures towards Noel while he played. He then spat beer all over the stage before storming off, actions that further damaged Oasis's reputation and prospects in the United States. "Liam deliberately sang off key. As Noel played, Liam gestured towards him in some kind of annoyed way. And then he spat beer all over the stage and stormed off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: MTV Unplugged No-Show – Noel Sings (August 23, 1996)
xref.body: Liam Gallagher backed out of an MTV Unplugged performance at the Royal Festival Hall at the last second, claiming a sore throat, which Noel dismissed as a hangover. With no time to cancel, Noel stepped up to sing the entire acoustic set himself, receiving positive reviews. Liam watched from the balcony, drinking beer and loudly heckling the band, even spitting beer towards the stage. "If you won't sing my songs, I will sing them. Noelle had already made an acoustic set part of the band show, so stepping up to sing the full set list wasn't that big of a deal for him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Response to Liam's MTV Unplugged No-Show (August 23, 1996)
xref.body: When Liam Gallagher claimed a sore throat to skip Oasis's MTV Unplugged performance, Noel angrily dismissed it as a hangover, declaring, "Bollocks do your throat, you're just hung over and you're being a prat." He then took over lead vocals for the entire set, performing his own songs. "'Right then, Bollocks do your throat, you're just hung over and you're being a prat. If you won't sing my songs, I will sing them.'"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Turbulent Royal Albert Hall Rehearsals (Mid-August 1996)
xref.body: In mid-August 1996, Oasis undertook "heavy-duty rehearsals" for their MTV Unplugged show at the Royal Albert Hall in London, under tight security. The rehearsals were marred by conflict, with brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher reportedly "came to blows several times," foreshadowing the disastrous taping. "So in mid-August of 1996, Oasis started some heavy-duty rehearsals under super tight security at Royal Albert Hall in London. Things did not go well. Nole and Liam came to blows several times."

xref.title: Barcelona Concert Cancellation & Paternity Question (2000)
xref.body: On May 20, 2000, Oasis was scheduled to perform in Barcelona, but the show was cancelled because drummer Alan White suffered from severe tendonitis in his hands and arms. This unexpected downtime led to significant drinking among the band members. During this period, Liam Gallagher made a disparaging comment about Noel Gallagher's then-wife, Meg Matthews, specifically questioning the paternity of their daughter, Anais. "On May 20th of that year, Oasis was supposed to perform in Barcelona. However, there was a problem. Former Alan White had bad tendonitis in his hands and arms, which is a very common thing for drummers. And there was no choice but to cancel the show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Barcelona Show Cancellation and Sibling Brawl (2000)
xref.body: On May 20th, 2000, an Oasis show in Barcelona was canceled because drummer Alan White suffered from severe tendonitis. During the band's unplanned downtime, Liam Gallagher made a derogatory remark about Noel's then-wife, Meg Matthews, questioning the paternity of their daughter, Anais. This led to Noel physically assaulting Liam, punching him in the face, splitting his lip, and delivering a serious headbutt, before declaring he quit the band. "At some point in the evening, Liam said something nasty about Null's then-wife Meg Matthews. Let's just say that he questioned the paternity of Null's daughter, Anase. This was a bad idea. Null leapt on Liam, punched him in the face, split his lip, and then gave him a serious headbutt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Noel Quits After Physical Altercation (2000)
xref.body: Following Liam Gallagher's comments questioning his daughter's paternity, Noel Gallagher physically assaulted Liam, punching him in the face, splitting his lip, and delivering a serious headbutt. Immediately after the altercation, Noel declared he quit the band, stating he was "done." "Noel leapt on Liam, punched him in the face, split his lip, and then gave him a serious headbutt. Then he stopped off saying that he quit. He was done with the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Noel's Temporary Departure (2000)
xref.body: After a physical altercation with Liam Gallagher in Barcelona, Noel Gallagher quit Oasis, leading the band to perform 18 subsequent shows without him. A replacement guitarist, Matt Deighton, played with the band in Milan on May 30th. Noel eventually returned on July 15th for UK outdoor festivals, though a press release stated he would no longer tour overseas with the band. "Null did not return to the band until July 15th when it was time to play some big outdoor festivals across the UK. And even then, a press release said that Null would no longer tour with a waste overseas."

xref.title: Consequences of Munich Brawl (2002)
xref.body: The fight, which began in the bar, escalated into the hotel lobby, resulting in broken furniture and smashed windows. Police responded with ten cars, finding Alan White bleeding from an ashtray blow to the head, and two security personnel injured, one of whom was unconscious. Liam Gallagher sustained significant injuries, losing several teeth and suffering extensive bruising. Despite his injuries, he resisted arrest by kicking a police officer in the ribs. Toxicology reports confirmed he was highly intoxicated with a substantial amount of cocaine in his system. "From the bar, the fight quickly moved out into the hotel lobby. Furniture was broken. Several windows were smashed. Hotel staff called the police, and they responded with ten cars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Financial and Legal Repercussions of Munich Brawl (2002)
xref.body: Liam Gallagher required $30,000 worth of emergency dental surgery following the Munich brawl. He and two other band members were jailed for 12 hours. The entire remaining European tour had to be cancelled, resulting in millions of dollars in lost revenue for the band. Additionally, management was forced to pay a fine exceeding $300,000 on Liam's behalf before any band member was permitted to leave Germany. Liam faced the possibility of two years in jail. "Liam required $30,000 worth of emergency dental surgery, and he and two other members of the band spent 12 hours in jail. Oh, and the rest of that European tour had to be cancelled, of course, costing the band millions in revenue. And if that weren't enough, management had to pay a fine on Liam's behalf of more than $300,000 before anybody in the band could leave Germany."

xref.title: Liam Walks Off Stage in Florida (2002)
xref.body: In August 2002, Liam Gallagher walked off stage during a Fort Lauderdale, Florida, show only four songs into the set, claiming his voice had failed due to the flu, which had previously caused a show cancellation in Spain. By the fall of that year, he had abandoned three other shows mid-set, contributing to significant tension within the band, including a six-week period where he and Noel did not speak. "In August 2002, Liam walked off the stage just four songs into a set in Fort Lauderdale Florida. He said his voice had gone bad, a continuation of a case of the flu that had caused a cancellation of a show in Spain 10 days earlier."

xref.title: Munich Bar Brawl (December 1, 2002)
xref.body: On December 1, 2002, while on tour supporting their album "Heathen Chemistry," Liam Gallagher, Alan White, and two other band members became heavily intoxicated at the nightclub bar of the Bayer Sherhoff hotel in Munich, Germany. They began throwing peanuts at five Italian individuals. When the DJ played an Oasis song, Liam and Alan White spontaneously jumped on stage for "unwanted karaoke." Subsequently, one of them (unclear if Liam or Alan) jumped on a table in front of the Italians, causing it to collapse and initiating a violent brawl. "It happened in a bar in Munich, Germany. This was December 1st, 2002. Oasis was on tour in support of their Heathen chemistry album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Munich Bar Brawl and Aftermath (2002)
xref.body: On December 1st, 2002, during a tour supporting "Heathen Chemistry," Liam Gallagher, Alan White, and two other band members became heavily intoxicated at the Bayer Sherhoff hotel bar in Munich, Germany. They provoked five Italians by throwing peanuts, and after an Oasis song played, Liam and Alan White jumped on stage for "unwanted karaoke." A fight erupted after one of them jumped on a table, causing it to collapse. The brawl escalated into the hotel lobby, resulting in broken furniture and smashed windows. Police arrived with ten cars to find Alan White bleeding from an ashtray to the head, and security details injured, one unconscious. Liam lost several teeth and was bruised, and was arrested after kicking a police officer. Toxicology confirmed his extreme intoxication and the presence of cocaine. Liam required $30,000 in emergency dental surgery, and he and two band members spent 12 hours in jail. The rest of the European tour was canceled, costing millions in revenue, and management paid over $300,000 for Liam to leave Germany. Noel, who was in his room during the incident, was furious upon learning of it. Liam could have faced two years in jail. "Liam had lost several teeth and was bruised and battered all over. The police spokesman was quoted as saying, the boy didn't look good. Several of his teeth were punched out. But that didn't stop him from launching himself at one of the cops kicking him in the ribs as hard as he could."

xref.title: Final Backstage Altercation in Paris (August 28, 2009)
xref.body: Five days after the V Festival cancellation, a final confrontation occurred backstage in Paris. Liam Gallagher, furious about negative press he believed Noel was involved in, ranted and threw a plum at the wall. He then returned with one of Noel's guitars, wielding it like an axe and swinging it violently, nearly striking Noel's head. The guitar was ultimately destroyed. "Five days later, they were in Paris, backstage in the dressing room. Liam was furious about the bad press he had been getting. Nothing to know. He began ranting and raving about all these people who were saying bad things about him, and that Noel had something to do with it. Liam wasn't apparently getting the sympathy he wanted from the rest of the band, so he starmed under the dressing room, throwing some fruit at the wall. A plumb, if you're interested."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liam's V Festival Cancellation and Slander Lawsuit (2009)
xref.body: Oasis was scheduled to perform at the V Festival on August 23, 2009, but Liam Gallagher cancelled the appearance, citing laryngitis. Two years later, Noel Gallagher publicly accused Liam of being massively hungover as the real reason for the cancellation, an accusation that prompted Liam to file a slander lawsuit against Noel, although the suit was later dropped. "The basis was supposed to play the V Festival in August 23rd, but Liam canceled because he had laryngitis. Two years later, Noel would claim that Liam was actually massively hungover, an accusation that caused Liam to sue his brother, but that suit was later dropped, more on that in a moment."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Paris Dressing Room Altercation and Oasis Breakup (2009)
xref.body: On August 28th, 2009, backstage in Paris, Liam Gallagher, enraged by negative press he attributed to Noel, stormed out of the dressing room, throwing a plum at the wall. He then returned, wielding one of Noel's guitars "like an axe" after Noel made a joke. Liam swung the guitar, narrowly missing Noel's head and ultimately trashing the instrument. Noel immediately left, and five minutes before showtime, announced he could no longer continue. Two hours later, a statement was posted on the Oasis website by Noel, confirming his departure due to his inability to work with Liam any longer, effectively ending Oasis after 18 years. "Noel left the dressing room in a huff, just as someone declared that it was five minutes to show time. Noel sat in a car backstage for all of those five minutes, and when he came out, he said, that's it. I can't do this anymore."

xref.body: The Oasis documentary "Super Sonic" had its premiere in London in October 2016. Liam Gallagher attended the event, but Noel Gallagher was notably absent. "In October 2016, the Oasis documentary Super Sonic had its premiere in London. Liam was there, but Noal wasn't."

xref.body: Noel Gallagher did not attend the premiere of the Oasis documentary "Super Sonic" in London in October 2016. Liam Gallagher publicly commented on his absence, suggesting Noel was in one of his large houses. "Liam was there, but Noal wasn't. Here's a quote from Liam. Oh no, he won't be there. He's in one of his really, really, really, really, really, really, really, really big houses. Probably in Tofu and having an effin' face pill. Isn't that right, men of the people?"

xref.title: Liam Open to Reunion (October 2016)
xref.body: During the premiere of the "Super Sonic" documentary in London in October 2016, Liam Gallagher expressed his openness to an Oasis reunion, despite ongoing public disputes with Noel. He emphasized the importance of people discussing Oasis as a band again, rather than just their conflicts. "But at the same time, Liam also said that he'd be open to an Oasis reunion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liam's Ambivalence Towards Reunion (2016)
xref.body: At the premiere of the Oasis documentary "Supersonic" in October 2016, Liam Gallagher acknowledged that it was good for people to be speaking about Oasis again, but he did not believe a reunion would result from the documentary or ongoing discussions. He cited his and Noel's busy schedules as a practical impediment. "I think it is good that people are speaking about Oasis, so I'll agree, but not about just being actually having a little bit of sheep and bigs at each other. So I think that's good that people are sort of speaking about us as a band again. But I don't think much of you're going to come from it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Sally Can Wait" Origin
xref.body: The phrase "Sally can wait" in "Don't Look Back In Anger" originated from Liam Gallagher mishearing Noel singing nonsense lyrics during a soundcheck. While Noel was merely keeping the melody with made-up words, Liam's question "are you saying Sally can wait?" prompted Noel to finish the lyrics in the dressing room. "And Liam asked, are you saying Sally can wait? And Noll says, I don't know what I'm singing."

xref.title: AI Version "AICIS" by Breezer
xref.body: A British band named Breezer, frustrated by the lack of an Oasis reunion, created an artificial intelligence version of the band called AICIS. This AI entity released an album, "The Lost Tapes Volume One," featuring AI-generated vocals resembling Liam Gallagher, which Liam himself reportedly found impressive. "A British band got so tired of waiting for an Oasis reunion that they brought in some artificial intelligence. They created an AI version of Oasis called AI CIS and released an album called The Lost Tapes Volume One."

xref.title: Liam Gallagher's Mummy Pose
xref.body: On the cover of Oasis's "Definitely Maybe" album, Liam Gallagher is seen lying on the floor in a pose reminiscent of an Egyptian mummy. xref.body: Lisa Moorish, a minor pop star, dated Liam Gallagher on and off for about two years and had an encounter with him in Los Angeles in June 1997, two months after his marriage to Patsy Kensit. "She was a minor pop star at the time. Liam and Lisa had dated on and off for about two years."

xref.title: Rumored Origin of Feud
xref.body: A rumor circulated that Damon Albarn had a one-night stand with a girl Liam Gallagher was seeing, which some consider the real catalyst for the feud, though Liam denied this. "And then there was the rumor that Damon was having a one night stand with a girl Liam was seeing. This did not help. And some might say that this was the real start of the feud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shaker Maker Lawsuit (The New Seekers)
xref.body: Oasis was sued by The New Seekers due to the melody of "Shaker Maker" sounding too similar to a Coca-Cola commercial jingle that The New Seekers had turned into a worldwide hit. Oasis did not strongly contest the claim, with Liam Gallagher often humorously inserting parts of the Coke commercial song into live performances of "Shaker Maker." The court ordered Oasis to make changes to the song. "The upshot of this was a court case and Oasis was ordered to make changes to the song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Battle of Britpop with Blur
xref.body: Oasis and Blur emerged around the same time in the mid-1990s and quickly became intense rivals, fueled by class differences (working-class Northerners vs. comparatively posh Southern university lads) and perceptions of authenticity. In February 1995, after Blur won four Brit Awards, Damon Albarn of Blur attempted to congratulate Oasis at their number one party for "Some Might Say," but Liam Gallagher confronted him with bragging. Noel Gallagher also made highly offensive remarks about Damon Albarn. "One of the greatest and most intense was the fight between Oasis and Blur in the middle 1990s. This was definitely real and undeniably ugly."

xref.title: Transition to Solo Career
xref.body: After releasing at least one more album (unspecified in the transcript) subsequent to "Different Gear Still Speeding," Liam Gallagher ultimately disbanded Beady Eye to launch a full-fledged solo career. "There was one more BDI album before Liam folded that tent with an idle launching of a full-on solo career."

xref.title: Tribute After Death
xref.body: Ozzy Osborne was among the many musicians who sent tributes upon Taylor Hawkins' death, underscoring the widespread respect and admiration he commanded from his peers. "When he died, tributes came in from everyone from Ozzy Osborne to Stevie Nicks, to Travis Barker, to Tom Morello to Liam Gallagher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unreleased MTV Unplugged CD and DVD
xref.body: As a direct consequence of Liam Gallagher's disruptive behavior during the MTV Unplugged performance and subsequent tour, the planned CD and DVD release of the Royal Albert Hall show was ultimately canceled. This resulted in the "lost Oasis unplugged album," largely featuring Noel Gallagher's vocals due to Liam's refusal to sing. "The upshot of all this chaos is that the planned CD and DVD of the Royal Albert Hall performance was never released. It's the lost, oasis unplugged album."

xref.title: Vocal Choice for Liam Gallagher
xref.body: For the recording of "Wonderwall," Noel Gallagher presented Liam with a choice between singing "Wonderwall" or "Don't Look Back In Anger," stating that Noel would sing whichever one Liam did not choose. Liam opted for "Wonderwall." "When it came to recording the vocals, Noll gave Liam a choice. You do this one or don't look back an anger. Whichever one you don't choose, I'll do."
